title: Scenario cards
subject: Computing
unit: Spring 1: Variables in games and e-bullying
source: Seeded from computing/y6 lesson 2 (Scenario cards (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 2: E-bullying: respond, block and report. To understand how to respond to e-bullying safely by blocking, reporting and telling

questions.q: Put in order: tell, block, stop, screenshot.
questions.model: Teacher explains each step's reason: stop (do not feed it), block (it cannot reach you), screenshot (proof), tell (an adult can act).

questions.a: Not on its own, but it is still wrong; repeated, on purpose, it is bullying.

questions.q: Name two trusted adults you could tell.
questions.a: For example: a parent and my class teacher.

questions.q: Core: Read the three scenarios. For each, write what to do using the four steps.
questions.a: Each answer uses stop, block, screenshot, tell; scenario 3 also includes being an upstander.

questions.q: Extend: Write a kind message an upstander could send to someone who was bullied, in the portal response box.
questions.a: For example: 'I saw what happened. It was not okay. I am here, and I have told a teacher.'

questions.q: Stretch: Discuss in your breakout pair: why might someone not tell? What would help them tell?
questions.a: Fear or embarrassment; knowing adults will help and it is not their fault.

questions.q: A screenshot is useful because... A) it is fun B) it keeps evidence C) it hides the message
Big question: is a mean comment online less hurtful? Give one reason.
questions.a: No: it can be seen by many people and saved.
